source.title: To understand deep learning we need to understand kernel learning
source.authors: Mikhail Belkin; Si-Yuan Ma; Soumik Mandal

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper experimentally studies analogous interpolation and generalization behavior in kernel classifiers and compares it conceptually with deep networks, but it does not test the network conditions or measures named by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's own kernel-classifier results are recorded under fits_no_version. Comparisons to ReLU networks in cited work are not rows. Kernel results do not measure the network behaviors specified by V1–V8.
record.test_reason: The study establishes analogous results for kernel classifiers and discusses their relevance to deep learning. It does not test any specified neural-network version. Viewing kernels as networks with a fixed first layer does not establish the architecture and training conditions named in V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors establish strong generalization by overfitted and interpolating kernel classifiers, including with substantial label noise, and parallels with reported deep-network behavior. They argue that existing kernel generalization bounds fail to explain these results and conjecture that structural kernel properties matter more than optimization specifics. Their minimum-norm inductive-bias explanation remains a proposed direction, not an established causal result.
record.recipe_differences: Kernel classifiers trained with EigenPro-SGD or direct minimum-norm interpolation; not neural networks or the original network training recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Kernel smoothness changes optimization difficulty: Laplacian kernels fit random labels in few epochs, while Gaussian kernels require many more. Early stopping yields at most a small or no performance improvement. Added label noise and dataset affect norms and test error.

fits_no_version.finding: Overfitted and interpolating kernel classifiers retain strong test performance across real and synthetic datasets. Early stopping generally provides little benefit, and performance remains near Bayes references under substantial label noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Kernel classifiers can interpolate training data while generalizing well, including under substantial label noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Laplacian kernels fit random labels in 7, 21 and 4 epochs on MNIST, SVHN and TIMIT; Gaussian kernels require 873, 1066 and 22 epochs. Their held-out performance is nevertheless similar.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Kernel smoothness can strongly affect random-label fitting effort without a corresponding difference in held-out performance.

record.problems: Test results are often presented in figures without exact values in the prose. Experiments use selected datasets and kernel methods; they do not directly test the neural-network versions. The authors state that the true Bayes risk for MNIST cannot be ascertained and use a zero-risk lower bound.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix B Tables 3–7 contain detailed kernel error values and data-size comparisons, but the supplied flattened formatting does not reliably associate all values with their methods, epochs, and conditions; no such uncertain reconstructions are included.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization in the specified neural architectures and recipes, including chance-level held-out accuracy with fully random labels.
Test error as neural-network width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected network performance and the contributions of locality, sparsity and initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, weight-decay changes or optimizer switching.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover held-out performance.
Dropout's effects on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps and competing measures within a convolutional family.
Retraining after removal of highly memorized examples versus removal of equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: T6 denotes no direct test or instrumental use of the specified versions; the paper discusses them through kernel analogies. States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8, not denials of the kernel findings. No uncovered result in the supplied text directly tests a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: The experiments use kernel classifiers, not the same neural-network architectures and recipes trained on natural versus random labels.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers and SGD on neural networks.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or comparison of generalization measures.
No removal of memorized training examples.

rows.subject: Gaussian kernel classifiers (EigenPro and direct interpolating solution)
rows.size_stated: Datasets include MNIST, CIFAR-10, SVHN (20k subsamples), TIMIT (50k subsamples), HINT-S (20k subsamples), and 20 Newsgroups; individual dataset sizes otherwise in Appendix A.
rows.operation_detail: Trained kernel classifiers across epochs; compared approximate EigenPro-SGD classifiers with direct interpolating solutions.

conditions.value: Six datasets listed in Section 3 and Figure 1

rows.measure: Test classification and regression error; training square loss approaches zero, and direct solutions interpolate.
rows.value: Test error is described as stable and, in most cases, decreasing and stabilizing; interpolated solutions are described as optimal or close to optimal on test.
rows.note: The paper reports an aggregate characterization across the displayed datasets; detailed values are in appendix tables, but the flattened table presentation does not support assigning every value to a method and epoch confidently.
rows.check: Kernel results cannot determine any listed version. This aggregate combines datasets, methods and measures; iterative Gaussian training does not reach zero classification error on HINT-S or 20 Newsgroups within 20 epochs, although direct interpolants do.

rows.operation_detail: Measured test classification error and RKHS norms for overfitted and interpolated classifiers with added label noise.

conditions.value: Synthetic dataset 1, separable classes with added noise

rows.measure: Test classification error and RKHS norm.
rows.baseline: Bayes optimal test error for the corresponding noise condition; numeric values are figure-only.
rows.note: Text states that classifiers perform at the Bayes-optimal level for 1% noise and slightly less accurately than Bayes optimal at 10% noise; precise plotted values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Synthetic kernel classification error and RKHS norms do not measure a listed version. The prose establishes near-Bayes performance, but exact figure values are unavailable in the supplied text.

rows.operation_detail: Measured test classification error and RKHS norms for overfitted and interpolated classifiers with added label noise.

conditions.value: Added label noise; exact plotted levels not stated in the supplied text

rows.measure: Test classification error and RKHS norm.
rows.baseline: Bayes optimal error approximately 15.9% before added noise.
rows.value: The interpolated classifier is stated to be consistently within 5% of Bayes optimal, even with added label noise.
rows.note: The paper describes the comparison in prose; specific plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: Near-Bayes performance of synthetic kernel classifiers does not measure a listed version. Preserve the authors' within-5% wording without interpreting it as a precise relative-error calculation.

rows.subject: Gaussian and Laplacian kernel classifiers
rows.size_stated: Synthetic-2 and MNIST; exact training sizes not stated for this figure.
rows.operation_detail: Compared test classification error of overfitted and interpolated classifiers with the Bayes-risk reference across added label-noise levels.

conditions.value: Different added-noise levels, including 80% label corruption

rows.baseline: Bayes risk; for MNIST the authors use a lower bound assuming zero Bayes risk.
rows.value: The classifiers are described as tracking Bayes risk and performing above chance even at 80% label corruption.
rows.note: Authors caution that the true Bayes risk for MNIST is unknown and likely slightly higher than the curve.
rows.check: Above-chance performance under 80% label corruption concerns kernel classifiers, not V1's neural networks or its fully random-label condition. MNIST's reference curve assumes zero underlying Bayes risk.
